source.title: On open problems of F. Qi

accepted.question_text: Let n be an integer at least 2, and let x_1, x_2, ..., x_n be nonnegative real numbers. Determine the best possible real exponents alpha_n and lambda_n and positive finite constants beta_n and mu_n, if such constants exist, for a two-sided inequality of the form beta_n sum_{i=1}^n x_i^{alpha_n} <= exp(sum_{i=1}^n x_i) <= mu_n sum_{i=1}^n x_i^{lambda_n} that is to hold for all such n-tuples of nonnegative real numbers.
accepted.context_brief: best constants in a finite exponential-sum inequality

evidence.quote: Problem 1.1. For (x1, x2, ..., xn) ∈[0, ∞)n and n ⩾2, determine the best possible constants αn, λn ∈R and βn > 0, µn < ∞ such that βn∑x_i^αn ≤ exp(∑x_i) ≤ µn∑x_i^λn.
we give a complete answer to Problem 1 and a partial answer to Problem 2 posed by F. Qi

accepted.question_text: Let [a,b] be a real interval and let f be a continuous function on [a,b]. Determine the integral analogue of the finite-sum two-sided inequality beta_n sum x_i^{alpha_n} <= exp(sum x_i) <= mu_n sum x_i^{lambda_n}; that is, formulate and determine best possible constants for a two-sided inequality comparing exp(integral_a^b |f(x)| dx) with an integral involving |f(x)|^p. The source records only a partial answer: for 0 < p <= 1, it proves the best-constant lower bound (e^p/p^p)(b-a)^{p-1} integral_a^b |f(x)|^p dx <= exp(integral_a^b |f(x)| dx).
accepted.context_brief: integral analogue of the exponential-sum inequality

evidence.quote: Problem 1.2. What is the integral analogue of the double inequality (1.5)?
In the following, we give a partial answer to Problem 1.2.
Let 0 < p ⩽1 be a real number, and let f be a continuous function on [a, b].

accepted.question_text: Let p be a real number with p >= 1, let [a,b] be a real interval, and let f be a continuous function on [a,b]. Determine the best possible real constant alpha such that the lower integral inequality (e^p/(p^p alpha)) integral_a^b |f(x)|^p dx <= exp(integral_a^b |f(x)| dx) holds in the setting stated by the source.
accepted.context_brief: best constant for the p >= 1 integral lower bound

evidence.quote: Problem 4.1. For p ≥1 a real number, determine the best possible constant α ∈R such that ep/(ppα)∫|f(x)|p dx ≤ exp(∫|f(x)| dx).
let f be a continuous function on [a, b]
